subject: MAP: Chat POC benchmarking playbook — TTFT & streaming latency plan

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Chat POC benchmarking playbook — TTFT & streaming latency plan

Hi Anika / Marco —

Per our kickoff today I put together the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focusing specifically on the performance/eval work for the chat/text-generation POC. Attached is a compact bench-plan.xlsx and the scripts bundle (ttft-scripts.tar.gz) we will use. High-level items: 

1) Scope & Success criteria (owner / due)
   - TTFT (time-to-first-token) cold start and warm (owner: Ben) / due: 2026-08-17
   - Streaming latency (p50/p95/p99) under realistic concurrency profiles (owner: Grace) / due: 2026-08-17
   - Throughput (tokens/sec) and sustained QPS at target concurrency (owner: Evelyn) / due: 2026-08-17
   - Acceptance: p95 streaming latency < 350ms on the preferred model during 95th percentile traffic for their test workload (owner: Acme) / target: 2026-08-18

2) Evaluation plan (test matrix)
   - Models: redwood-chat-3b-quant, redwood-chat-7b-fp16, open-llama-chat-7b (as baseline)
   - Workloads: demo traffic (5–10 prompts/min), scale tests (concurrency 1, 8, 32, 128)
   - Metrics: TTFT (p50/p95/p99), streaming token latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, error rate, GPU util, end-to-end tail latency

3) Environment / constraints
   - Tests run from Acme staging VPC -> Redwood Dedicated region-us-west2; we will use the sample dataset you shared (chat-sessions-aug.json)
   - Network egress and cold-cache paths included; will run both cold restart and steady-state runs

4) Deliverables
   - Raw CSVs + summarized PDF (bench result + plots)
   - Runner scripts and Jupyter notebook for reproducibility
   - Short executive summary for your SLT

Next steps: Please confirm the acceptance criteria above and the week-of-aug-17 target for final results. If agreed, Ben/Grace/Evelyn will schedule runs across two windows (prelim: Aug 9–11; final: Aug 15–17).

Thanks,
Rohan

--

Thanks Rohan — this looks good and aligned with our internal goals. A couple of quick notes from Acme SRE/Product: 

- Success criteria: our product lead wants p95 streaming latency < 300ms for common prompt sizes (~60 tokens). p95 < 350ms is acceptable as fallback.
- We’ll provide the staged workload and a small holdback set to verify regressions.
- We prefer runs during our quieter window (start 0200-0600 UTC) to limit interference.

Confirming acceptance of the proposed Aug 9–11 preliminary window and Aug 15–17 final window.

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 22:15:00 -0700
Subject: Results: TTFT & streaming latency summary (prelim + final runs)

Hi all —

Attached are the raw CSVs (acme-ttft-results.csv) and a short PDF with plots (acme-streaming-summary.pdf). Below is an executive summary with key numbers from the final runs (Aug 15–17) — streaming numbers are end-to-end from client emulator in Acme staging VPC to Redwood response stream. Values are in milliseconds unless noted.

Test config: redwood-chat-7b-fp16:v2026-07-30; steady-state cache primed; runs repeated 5x, reported percentiles across all runs. Concurrency levels: 1, 8, 32, 128. Prompts ~60 tokens, average response token length 80.

TTFT (time-to-first-token) — cold start runs (mean across 5 full restarts):
- p50: 420ms
- p95: 1,120ms
- p99: 1,900ms

TTFT — warm (steady-state, primed KV cache):
- p50: 58ms
- p95: 95ms
- p99: 160ms

Streaming token latency (per-token streaming time; end-to-end) — redwood-chat-7b-fp16:v2026-07-30
Concurrency 1:
- token p50: 18ms, p95: 46ms, p99: 92ms
Concurrency 8:
- token p50: 22ms, p95: 72ms, p99: 160ms
Concurrency 32:
- token p50: 28ms, p95: 140ms, p99: 320ms
Concurrency 128:
- token p50: 45ms, p95: 520ms, p99: 1,260ms

Notes / interpretation:
- Warm TTFT and per-token streaming p95 meet Acme's target for low concurrency (1–8). Under sustained high concurrency (32+), tail increases significantly — we observed GPU queuing and KV cache pressure.
- Cold-start TTFT is higher than desired; we recommend a mini warm pool (reserved warm instances) for production if p95 cold-start < 350ms is required.
- Throughput: sustained tokens/sec at concurrency 32 ~ 9.2k tokens/sec (aggregate across all workers); single-stream throughput was ~95 tokens/sec.

Proposed follow-ups in MAP:
- If Acme wants p95 streaming < 350ms at concurrency 32, we can trial a 2x instance sizing or targeted batching changes (owner: Grace) / ETA: Aug 25
- Warm pool experiment (owner: Ben) / ETA: Aug 22

Ben
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Anika Shah <anika.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@sre.acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Results: TTFT & streaming latency summary (prelim + final runs)

Thanks Ben — very helpful and disciplined runs. A few decisions from our side: 

- We accept the current perf for low concurrency; for peak traffic we want Redwood to try the warm-pool experiment and the 2x sizing test. Please schedule the experiments and we will provide a small budget for the dedicated warm pool during the trial.
- Requesting a short 1-pager (decision memo) that quantifies cost delta vs latency improvement for the two options above. ETA for memo: Aug 24.

If you can own the trials (Grace/Ben) and Rohan can loop in procurement for the temporary capacity budget, we can mark the MAP milestone 'performance acceptance' as pending experiments.

Anika
